newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares fall to lowest level since January.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares fall to lowest level since January.

text.p: Egyptian share prices plummeted on Sunday to their lowest level in six months but volume was high due to the state's latest privatisation.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index fell 2.57 points to 350, its lowest level since the 346.58 points it reached on January 21.
Turnover, however, was an above-average 100.28 million pounds ($29.5 million), buoyed by the state's sale of 49.5 million pounds worth of shares in Simo/Middle East Paper.
The government last week offered investors up to 2.25 million shares or 75 percent of the firm at a minimum price of 20 pounds per share. It sold all the shares on offer at 22 pounds each.
Brokers said the privatisation was the highlight of Sunday's market which they said was degenerating into speculation.

"Everybody's jumping on the selling bandwagon to drive the prices down until they bottom out and then can buy the stocks at cheaper prices. Even the Egyptian mutual funds are speculating now and their effect is pretty strong on the market," said broker Walid el-Khouli at El-Rashad Securities Brokerage.
"There's really no reason for the prices to fall, investors just cannot support the market or they don't want to," he added.
Khouli said many shares had become undervalued, and that had encouraged foreign investors and some institutions to buy into the real estates, chemicals and banking sectors.
But the day's two most active firms -- Alexandria National Iron and Steel (ANSDK) and Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles -- ended lower, dragging the market down with them.
ANSDK closed 13 pounds down at 247 pounds after shares worth 6.2 million changed hands while Kabo, the most heavily traded share with more than 10 million pounds of turnover, fell 2.0 to 106 pounds.
Brokers said investors were scooping up share blocs in Commercial International Bank (CIB), PACHIN/Paints and Chemical Industries and Medinet Nasr Housing and Development.
CIB rose 1.04 to 71.94 pounds, PACHIN gained 0.14 to 116.2 pounds while Medinet Nasr climbed 2.0 pounds to 236.
Cement firms were active on Sunday, with Helwan Portland Cement HELW.CA rising 0.85 pounds to 71.35 and Amriya Cement gaining 0.5 to 82.
Sunday's public offer of at least 10 percent of Alexandria Flour Mills had little effect on the popular milling sector which closed mostly down in thin volume.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 479.71 points from 485.06 points on Thursday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms also slipped to 258.75 from 260.15 points.
Of the 97 shares traded, 26 rose, 42 fell while 29 ended unchanged.
